prompt: The distribution of inputs $P(X)$ changes but $P(Y\mid X)$ stays the same. This is...
explanation: Covariate shift: same input-to-label relation, different inputs.

prompt: Houses with the same features now sell for less after a market change. This is...
explanation: $P(Y\mid X)$ changed while $P(X)$ did not: same input, different output.

prompt: A feature's mean is unchanged but its variance doubled. Which statement is true?
options: A mean comparison and KS/PSI would all miss it
It cannot be a distribution shift
A mean comparison misses it; KS and PSI detect it
explanation: Means ignore spread; the CDF gap and the binned PSI both change when the shape changes.

prompt: Reference proportions in one PSI bin are $p=0.10$ and the new proportion is $q=0.20$. What is that bin's PSI term $(q-p)\ln(q/p)$? (natural log, 3 decimals)
Observability, as opposed to monitoring, is about...
options: instrumenting the system so you can investigate why something went wrong
explanation: Monitoring tracks metrics; observability is the instrumentation that makes causes visible, and monitoring depends on it.

prompt: Stateful training differs from stateless retraining in that it...
options: continues from the previous checkpoint using only new data
trains from scratch on all data
explanation: Fine-tuning from the last checkpoint needs less data and compute.

prompt: Arm A: 100 clicks out of 1,000. Arm B: 130 clicks out of 1,000. What is the pooled two-proportion $z$ statistic (2 decimals)?
You check an A/B test daily and stop at the first $|z|>1.96$. The false-positive rate (when A and B are identical) is...
explanation: Each look gives noise another chance to cross the threshold; with ten looks it is about 20% in our simulation.
